requirements.title: First-year preparation
requirements.summary: Four years of English, three of social studies, four of mathematics including algebra, geometry, trigonometry and precalculus; calculus preferred. Two to three years of science including chemistry or physics, both preferred. Computing is preferred.

requirements.title: Transfer preparation
requirements.summary: At least precalculus and chemistry or physics; computing courses are preferred. Internal transfers are accepted; students beyond the first two years should consult an advisor about remaining time.

requirements.title: Undergraduate transfer approval
requirements.summary: Transfer courses require institutional approval and a C or better. Previously evaluated credit applies only where it fits the chosen program. Enrolled degree students need prior written approval from the home dean/director or designee for outside coursework; applicable residency limits still apply.

requirements.title: Minor/major grading and noncredit limits
requirements.summary: Elected Pass/No Pass is limited to open electives and cannot satisfy a major, minor, general education or immersion requirement. X grades carry earned credit but no GPA or residency credit; audit and failed courses do not satisfy undergraduate residency. S-graded study abroad may carry residency and earned credit but no GPA; other undergraduate S categories do not carry credit or residency.

requirements.title: Repeated undergraduate courses
requirements.summary: The last grade earned in a repeated undergraduate course is final, even when lower. Outside courses and examination/experience credit cannot repeat prior coursework. Repeated or excluded coursework is annotated and excluded from the applicable prior GPA calculation.

requirements.title: Applicable undergraduate catalog
requirements.summary: Requirements normally follow the bulletin at program matriculation; a later advantageous bulletin may be chosen. The graduation bulletin cannot be more than seven calendar years old. Discontinued courses are not guaranteed; individual adjustments require the primary department head’s approval.

requirements.title: University graduation requirements
requirements.summary: Complete all required university and college courses, including applicable cooperative work; record all grades and resolve incompletes. A cumulative GPA of at least 2.00 is required.

requirements.title: Baccalaureate residency
requirements.summary: At least 25 percent of the degree’s total semester credit hours must be successfully completed RIT courses. The degree-granting program decides which specific courses qualify.

requirements.title: University baccalaureate minimum
requirements.summary: A baccalaureate degree requires at least 120 credit hours or the higher college/program total. This university floor does not replace the AI program’s published total.

requirements.title: Wellness, writing and administrative completion
requirements.summary: Complete the published wellness requirements and university writing competency requirements (D01.5). Financial obligations must be paid or satisfactorily adjusted; degree candidates are expected to attend commencement. The detailed D01.5 writing structure is represented separately.

requirements.title: Three writing-intensive courses
requirements.summary: Complete three credit-bearing writing-intensive courses within the degree: first-year FYW Writing Seminar or a designated three-credit FYW alternative approved by its director; a WI-PR course or sequence in the degree program; and a third WI course, ideally general education but permitted to be another WI-PR. Recommended year spacing is not a mandatory semester order. Exact AI-program WI designations still need verification.

requirements.title: BS general education distribution
requirements.summary: The BS general-education framework totals at least 60 semester hours: three First-Year Writing, 24 Perspectives, nine Immersion and remaining general-education electives (the framework table shows 24). These hours are part of the published degree total, not 60 additional hours.

requirements.title: Eight perspective courses across seven categories
requirements.summary: Complete one course in each of Ethical, Artistic, Global, Social, Natural Science Inquiry and Scientific Principles, plus two Mathematical Perspective courses. These eight courses fulfill the perspective distribution; program-designated courses can cover existing slots. A BS program may prescribe specific courses in no more than three perspective categories.

requirements.title: Primary-discipline general education limit
requirements.summary: At most three required courses, excluding laboratories, from the program’s primary discipline may count toward general education, and they must have approved General Education designation. Do not assume that every AI/computing course qualifies.

requirements.title: Immersion declaration and no program overlap
requirements.summary: Complete and declare an approved immersion of at least three related general-education courses totaling at least nine credits. Immersion courses may complement the major but cannot overlap program requirements. Programs cannot require one particular immersion or restrict the immersion group. A minor is optional and does not automatically satisfy an immersion.

requirements.title: Approved first-year writing alternatives
requirements.summary: The current university page lists UWRT-150 FYW: Writing Seminar and ISTE-110 FYW: Ethics in Computing as approved first-year writing courses. Other designated three-credit FYW alternatives require the program director’s approval. This general permission does not silently replace a more specific degree-course requirement.

requirements.title: Wellness exemptions, transfer and experiential credit
requirements.summary: The two required wellness activities must differ in activity or level. Exemptions cover age 25 or older at matriculation, six months of active military service, an earlier bachelor degree, or non-matriculated status. Medical exemption requires licensed-provider documentation and authorized approval with both academic and wellness offices. Transfer wellness work requires department review; varsity seasons earn wellness activity credit. Final-semester prior learning or certification may count with Wellness Education approval. Club and intramural sports do not count.

requirements.title: Degree requirements and typical sequence charts
requirements.summary: The university graduation page directs students to catalog requirements and recognizes WI designations on typical sequence charts. The public 2026–27 AI chart now explicitly labels IDAI-490 WI-PR. It remains a typical sequence with unresolved source conflicts, not a completed degree audit.

requirements.title: Program writing-intensive designation
requirements.summary: The 2026–27 School of Information flowchart explicitly marks IDAI-490 AI Team Capstone as WI-PR and requires fourth-year standing. It separately shows first-year writing and an additional Writing Intensive checkbox; these fit the existing university three-course structure, not extra credits.

requirements.title: Advising elective list differs from catalog
requirements.summary: The 2026–27 advising PDF says to select two three-credit AI electives. It lists CSCI-431; EEEE-485 OR CSCI-632; LING-582; LING-584; SWEN-566; PUBL-550. The separately captured catalog instead uses CSCI-634 for robotics and omits the two linguistics options. These source-specific options are retained as conflicting evidence, not combined into one approved pool.

requirements.title: Independent advising chart and immersion ambiguity
requirements.summary: The 2026–27 flowchart shows three separate immersion slots and labels MATH-190 as discrete mathematics, without an immersion designation. It therefore does not establish an exception to the university no-program-overlap rule or resolve the captured catalog’s extra Immersion 3 annotation.

requirements.title: Conditional course enrollment
requirements.summary: Undergraduates must satisfy prerequisites for approved 100–500-level courses. Courses outside their usual plan require the offering department’s approval. Graduate-level courses may count when they fit the bachelor schedule and both home and offering departments approve. These are conditional routes, not granted waivers, automatic equivalents or added fixed courses.

requirements.title: Registration and independent study
requirements.summary: Ordinary add/drop lasts seven calendar days excluding Sundays/holidays; exceptional later changes require signed approval. Independent study requires a written proposal, agreed credits, faculty/administrative approval and evaluation. College/department limits and degree applicability remain locally determined.

requirements.title: Conditional cross-registration
requirements.summary: Rochester-area cross-registration requires full-time home enrollment, a needed course unavailable at home, degree relevance and available space. It excludes summer, graduate students and graduate courses; host academic rules apply. Associated fees or overload charges may remain.

requirements.title: First-year writing exemption and source-specific alternatives
requirements.summary: The UWP student page permits an approved first-year writing transfer course or an AP Language and Composition score of 3 or better to satisfy FYW. UWRT150 remains the AI sequence course. The FAQ names an online ISTE150 section for selected students, while the same page’s prize section and university graduation page name ISTE110; this is preserved as an unresolved code discrepancy, not an inferred replacement or additional fixed course.

requirements.title: Current writing-intensive approval inventory
requirements.summary: The Writing Committee directs students to the WRTG attribute in SIS for current approved offerings. Its dated-list reference is placeholder text with no document link. UWP descriptions of UWRT150, UWRT325 and UWRT365 do not by themselves certify that those courses exhaust or belong to the current additional-WI pool. The university three-course WI requirement remains within existing degree hours.

requirements.title: Exceptional general-education WI substitution timing
requirements.summary: The public UWP page says GE WI substitutions are rarely granted and requires a petition and writing portfolio. It will not consider last-minute petitions after the two weeks prior to graduation. Planning and an advance graduation audit with the advisor are advised; approval is not assumed.

requirements.title: Conditional GE writing-intensive substitution evidence
requirements.summary: The currently linked two-page form permits consideration of an already completed approved GE course passed with C or better, including accepted transfer GE credit. The advisor confirms that no WI-GE course has been taken and other GE credit requirements are fulfilled; the home department confirms a compelling case and submits the portfolio. The portfolio must include a reasoned letter, course syllabus/assignment evidence, final writing and a transcript; evidence must show formal revision with feedback, informal writing, distributed writing instruction and at least 20 percent of the course grade for writing. The UWP director has sole discretion, with no further direct appeal; submission does not guarantee approval or change earned/required credits or GPA. The PDF’s deadline fields are blank, so timing is taken only from the separately reviewed current web page.

requirements.title: Historical science recommendation list is not a current pool
requirements.summary: The science-perspectives document linked by the current GE FAQ expressly lists approvals as of March 2013 and directs readers to SIS for current information. Its codes are not promoted into the 2026–2027 AI degree’s current approved GE pool.

requirements.title: Approved immersion route — partially observed menu
requirements.summary: Students choose and declare an approved immersion under university policy. All 77 published route rules have been reviewed in the route queue; three branches currently have represented course records here. The 714 remaining named identifiers need actual course content, and Global Experience is approval-based rather than a finite menu. No default selection, singleton promotion or full course-inventory claim is intended.

requirements.title: Mathematics immersion: choose three eligible courses
requirements.summary: Conditional Mathematics Immersion route, not additional universal AI core: choose three eligible electives from the source-listed menu, including at least one at the 300-level or above. Selection row publishes 9–12 semester hours and total row shows 9; actual selected-course amounts must be preserved. University and route policy prohibit overlap with program requirements, so the AI-required MATH241/251 cannot be reused to satisfy this route. They are retained in the source manifest but excluded from this AI-specific choice node; no exception is asserted. The route is closed to applied/computational mathematics majors.

requirements.title: Mathematics immersion preparation is separate
requirements.summary: The source separates prerequisites from the three immersion electives: first choose MATH181 or the MATH171+172 sequence; then its second prerequisite list includes MATH182, MATH173, MATH190 and MATH200. These are preparation/entry observations, not extra fixed AI degree requirements or immersion-credit choices. Individual course prerequisites, grades and equivalents still apply.

requirements.title: Mathematics immersion exclusions and approvals
requirements.summary: Footnotes prohibit selecting both MATH219/221 or both MATH231/233. MATH221H also excludes credit with 219/221 in its own description; no same-course identity is inferred. Honors221H/241H use a 3.2 GPA alternative, while 367H uses 3.3. MATH233 explicitly restricts enrollment to CHEM-BS, CHEM-BS/MS or ISEE-BS; an AI student would need the separately documented departmental permission route, not an assumed waiver. Legacy prerequisite numbers and Boolean wording are retained as published.

requirements.title: AI in Society immersion: conditional nine-hour route
requirements.summary: One optional declared immersion route within existing GE hours: complete STSO320 and two listed electives. It may complement the AI degree but may not overlap program requirements; it is not a universal AI core requirement or an additional credential requirement.

requirements.title: Choose two AI in Society electives
requirements.summary: Choose two of the thirteen listed courses. Every current card separately states three credits; individual amounts were not inferred by dividing the six-hour group.

requirements.title: Applied Statistics immersion: choose three eligible courses
requirements.summary: Conditional APSTAT-IM branch: choose three source-listed electives, including at least one at 300 level or above. The published 14-code pool includes MATH-251, but that fixed AI requirement cannot also satisfy immersion, leaving 13 AI-eligible choices before individual enrollment/credit conditions. Closed to applied statistics and data analytics majors. STAT-205 and STAT-257 cannot both receive credit. This is one optional immersion, not additional universal AI core.

requirements.title: Applied Statistics preparation and course-entry conditions
requirements.summary: The route separately lists MATH-181 and MATH-182 as preparation, not immersion electives. They are existing fixed AI courses, not two new obligations. Published individual prerequisites and credit exclusions still apply; equivalent-course clauses are conditional, not granted waivers. STAT-325 has published WI-GE and WI-Program attributes, without a guarantee of a particular term offering.
